title: Stock market today: Dow erases losses to end positive, S&P 500 and Nasdaq recover ground amid AI sell-off
summary:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) gained 0.3%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) dropped 0.2%.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell about 0.6% as Wall Street's anxiety over inflation and the AI trade weighed on equities.
Semiconductor stocks fell, with Nvidia (NVDA) shares losing nearly 4%, trimming earlier losses.
The Trump administration, meanwhile, unveiled new 20% tariffs targeting China, the European Union, and 12 other major US trading partners.
The stock and bond markets will be closed tomorrow in observance of Thanksgiving and will reopen Friday for a half-day of trading.

title: Fed's favored inflation gauge heats up, solidifying a rate hike in December, with more likely next year
summary:
Month over month, core prices held steady at 0.3%, in line with projections.
Month over month, PCE moderated, rising 0.3% as expected and down from 0.5% previously.
"The continued strength in core PCE inflation … make[s] a December rate hike certain," said Bradley Saunders, economist for Capital Economics.
Services price growth was also strong, up 0.28% month over month, led by recreational services and food and accommodation services.
Most Fed officials have already coalesced around a rate hike next month, though some have called for more aggressive action than others.

title: Inflation: How rising food prices are squeezing Indian households
summary:
Rice prices were up about 10% year-on-year, pulses 8%, edible oil 13% and LPG 10%, according to Pushan Sharma, director of intelligence at Crisil.
And food inflation is not just about what farmers produce.
Weaknesses at each stage can turn seasonal shortages into sharp price spikes - and gluts into waste.
Tomatoes, meanwhile, tend to see price spikes during the summer months, when arrivals decline in some markets or heat stress affects production.
Tomatoes, for example, can become so abundant during a glut that farmers struggle to sell them at remunerative prices, only for consumers to face sharply higher prices months later.

title: With the rise of AI, are we close to having universal basic income
summary:

But is the solution giving people universal basic income just for existing?
Al Jazeera’s Yasmeen ElTahan explains.

title: Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy?
summary:
Share Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy?
on social mediaAs rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI) raise fears of mass job losses, calls for the rollout of universal basic income (UBI) are gaining traction.
In his view, a basic income could make job losses easier to accept as people are more likely to tolerate AI replacing their work if they are being paid.
In a scenario where AI leads to mass layoffs, people will have less money to spend.
From this perspective, UBI would function less as a form of charity than as a way to keep consumer spending going.

summary:
Elon Musk is going galactic with his latest claim of what SpaceX might be worth one day: $128 quintillion.
That's 128 billion billions, or 128 trillion millions, or 128 followed by 18 zeros: 128,000,000,000,000,000,000.

title: Fed's preferred gauge of inflation climbs ahead of possible rate hike
summary:
The Federal Reserve's preferred gauge of inflation climbed in October, according to a government report issued on Wednesday.
The measure is sure to draw attention from central bankers as they weigh a possible rate increase early next month.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index (PCE) showed annual inflation climbed from 3.6% in September to 3.8% in October.
The report arrived weeks after a separate inflation measure, the Consumer Price Index (CPI), showed a larger jump in prices in October than economists had expected.
Wall Street will also take notice of the PCE report after a volatile stretch of trading.

title: South Korea’s central bank hikes interest rates amid AI chip boom
summary:
Bank of Korea raises key rate by 0.25 percent amid booming exports of semiconductors.
South Korea’s central bank has hiked interest rates as red-hot chip demand drives one of the Asian economy’s fastest expansions in more than a decade.
The Bank of Korea (BOK) on Thursday raised its key rate by 0.25 percent to 3.25 percent, citing strong domestic growth and above-target inflation.
South Korea’s exports rose 94 percent year-on-year in October to reach $115.3bn, following an all-time monthly record of $120.9bn in September.
After a tech-led sell-off the previous day, South Korea’s stock market rose on Thursday alongside a rebound in equities across the region.

title: Fast Fashion Fiasco: Shein to Pay $100 Million in FTC Complaint
summary:
The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase issues and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.
In 2026, the company is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC.
That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.
According to Yale Climate Connections, the company emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023.
Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

title: Oil prices rise after Houthis claim attack on Saudi refinery
summary:
By Nicole Jao and Anna HirtensteinNEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Crude oil prices rallied on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle ‌East supply disruptions that could cut against expectations for a coming global surplus.
Brent crude futures settled $3.21, or 3.5%, ‌higher at $94.61 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed $1.63, or 2%, to $83.68.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ​said on Wednesday that they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district.
The refinery, Saudi Arabia's largest, is part of a complex that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.
The Houthi statement triggered Wednesday's price rally, said PVM oil analyst Tamas Varga, citing a rising geopolitical risk premium.
